> ## The Hook
>
> > **Across the entities in this dataset, the headline indicator (**Unemployment_Pct**) moved **-1.6%** between 2022 and 2024.**
>
> This report turns those numbers into a narrative: where Europe started, what changed, what the data reveals, and what it implies for the road ahead.
>
> ## The Context: Where Europe Started
>
> - **8 entities/regions** tracked in this dataset.
> - Data spans **2022 to 2024**.

> | Netherlands | 2022–2024 | 54 | 3.8 (2024) |

> ## The Conflict: Divergence in the Numbers
>

>
> | Entity | Change (%) | Latest value | Year |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | Sweden | 12.0% | 8.4 | 2024 |
> | Germany | 9.7% | 3.4 | 2024 |
> | Netherlands | 8.6% | 3.8 | 2024 |

> | Spain | -12.4% | 11.3 | 2024 |
> | Italy | -14.8% | 6.9 | 2024 |
>
> - **5 entity/entities improved** (median change 8.6%).
> - **3 entity/entities weakened** (median change -12.4%).
> - This **divergence is the central tension** of the European story: gains in some economies are offset by losses elsewhere.
>
> ## The Insight: What the Data Reveals
>
> Digging deeper into the numbers surfaces three patterns:
>
> 1. **The standout performer is Germany** — Unemployment_Pct moved from 3.1 (2022) to 3.4 (2024), a **9.7%** swing.
> 2. **The laggard is Italy** — Unemployment_Pct went from 8.1 (2022) to 6.9 (2024), a **-14.8%** change.
> 3. **The range of outcomes is wide** — across all entities, the spread between best and worst change is **24.5 percentage points**, signaling that European performance is shaped by local conditions, not a single trend.
>
> ### Year-by-year movement (headline indicator)
>
> | Entity | 2022 | 2024 |
> |---|---|---|
> | EU | 6.2 | 6.1 |
> | France | 7.3 | 7.5 |

> | Italy | 8.1 | 6.9 |
> | Netherlands | 3.5 | 3.8 |
> | Poland | 2.9 | 3 |
> | Spain | 12.9 | 11.3 |
> | Sweden | 7.5 | 8.4 |
>
> The pattern becomes clear when we stop looking at averages and compare **who is pulling Europe up** versus **who is holding it back**.
>
> ## The Resolution: What This Implies
>
> Based on the observed data:
>
> 1. **Benchmark against the leaders.** The gap between the top and bottom performers is the single most actionable number in this dataset — closing even part of it would lift the European average meaningfully.
> 2. **Watch the direction of travel.** The latest-year values set the baseline for the next cycle; early signals in the most recent period deserve the closest monitoring.
> 3. **Treat the region as a portfolio.** Divergent outcomes mean a one-size-fits-all read of 'Europe' hides as much as it reveals — segment the analysis by entity before making decisions.
>

>

arguments.content:
import csv

rows = []
with open("eu_economic_data.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    for r in reader:
        rows.append({k.strip(): (v.strip() if isinstance(v, str) else v) for k, v in r.items()})

countries = ["Germany", "France", "Italy", "Spain", "Netherlands", "Poland", "Sweden"]
years = ["2022", "2023", "2024"]
metrics = ["GDP_Billion_EUR", "GDP_Growth_Pct", "Unemployment_Pct", "Inflation_Pct",
           "Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR", "Public_Debt_Pct_GDP"]

def get(country, year):
    for r in rows:
        if r["Country"] == country and r["Year"] == year:
            return r
    raise KeyError((country, year))

print("=" * 78)
print("EU TOTAL SNAPSHOT")
print("=" * 78)
eu = {y: get("EU_Total", y) for y in years}
for y in years:
    r = eu[y]
    print(f"{y}: GDP {r['GDP_Billion_EUR']} Bn | growth {r['GDP_Growth_Pct']}% | "
          f"unemp {r['Unemployment_Pct']}% | infl {r['Inflation_Pct']}% | "
          f"trade {r['Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR']} Bn | debt {r['Public_Debt_Pct_GDP']}%")

g_22_24 = (float(eu["2024"]["GDP_Billion_EUR"]) / float(eu["2022"]["GDP_Billion_EUR"]) - 1) * 100
print(f"\nNominal GDP growth 2022->2024 (EU total): {g_22_24:.1f}%")
print(f"Disinflation 2022->2024: {float(eu['2022']['Inflation_Pct']) - float(eu['2024']['Inflation_Pct']):.1f} pts")
print(f"Trade balance swing 2022->2024: {float(eu['2024']['Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR']) - float(eu['2022']['Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR']):+.1f} Bn")
print(f"Debt reduction 2022->2024: {float(eu['2022']['Public_Debt_Pct_GDP']) - float(eu['2024']['Public_Debt_Pct_GDP']):.1f} pts")

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("COUNTRY RANKINGS (2024)")
print("=" * 78)
print(f"{'Country':<12}{'GDP':>12}{'Growth24':>10}{'Unemp24':>9}{'Infl24':>8}{'Trade24':>11}{'Debt24':>9}")
for c in sorted(countries, key=lambda c: -float(get(c, "2024")["GDP_Billion_EUR"])):
    r = get(c, "2024")
    print(f"{c:<12}{r['GDP_Billion_EUR']:>12}{r['GDP_Growth_Pct']:>10}{r['Unemployment_Pct']:>9}"
          f"{r['Inflation_Pct']:>8}{r['Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR']:>11}{r['Public_Debt_Pct_GDP']:>9}")

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("GROWTH STORY PER COUNTRY (real GDP growth, %)")
print("=" * 78)
print(f"{'Country':<12}{'2022':>8}{'2023':>8}{'2024':>8}{'Cumulative(22-24)':>18}")
for c in countries:
    g22 = float(get(c, "2022")["GDP_Growth_Pct"])
    g23 = float(get(c, "2023")["GDP_Growth_Pct"])
    g24 = float(get(c, "2024")["GDP_Growth_Pct"])
    cum = ((1 + g22/100) * (1 + g23/100) * (1 + g24/100) - 1) * 100
    print(f"{c:<12}{g22:>8.1f}{g23:>8.1f}{g24:>8.1f}{cum:>18.1f}")

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("UNEMPLOYMENT CHANGE 2022->2024 (pts)")
print("=" * 78)
for c in sorted(countries, key=lambda c: float(get(c, "2024")["Unemployment_Pct"])):
    d = float(get(c, "2024")["Unemployment_Pct"]) - float(get(c, "2022")["Unemployment_Pct"])
    print(f"{c:<12}2022: {get(c,'2022')['Unemployment_Pct']:>5} -> 2024: {get(c,'2024')['Unemployment_Pct']:>5}  ({d:+.1f})")

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("DISINFLATION 2022->2024 (pts, larger = bigger drop)")
print("=" * 78)
for c in sorted(countries, key=lambda c: -(float(get(c, "2022")["Inflation_Pct"]) - float(get(c, "2024")["Inflation_Pct"]))):
    d = float(get(c, "2022")["Inflation_Pct"]) - float(get(c, "2024")["Inflation_Pct"])
    print(f"{c:<12}2022: {get(c,'2022')['Inflation_Pct']:>5} -> 2024: {get(c,'2024')['Inflation_Pct']:>5}  ({d:+.1f})")

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("TRADE BALANCE CHANGE 2022->2024 (Bn EUR)")
print("=" * 78)
for c in sorted(countries, key=lambda c: -float(get(c, "2024")["Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR"])):
    d = float(get(c, "2024")["Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR"]) - float(get(c, "2022")["Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR"])
    print(f"{c:<12}2022: {get(c,'2022')['Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR']:>7.1f} -> 2024: {get(c,'2024')['Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR']:>7.1f}  ({d:+.1f})")

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("PUBLIC DEBT CHANGE 2022->2024 (pts of GDP)")
print("=" * 78)
for c in sorted(countries, key=lambda c: -float(get(c, "2024")["Public_Debt_Pct_GDP"])):
    d = float(get(c, "2024")["Public_Debt_Pct_GDP"]) - float(get(c, "2022")["Public_Debt_Pct_GDP"])
    print(f"{c:<12}2022: {get(c,'2022')['Public_Debt_Pct_GDP']:>6.1f} -> 2024: {get(c,'2024')['Public_Debt_Pct_GDP']:>6.1f}  ({d:+.1f})")

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("CONTEXT CALCULATIONS")
print("=" * 78)
ger_share = float(get("Germany", "2024")["GDP_Billion_EUR"]) / float(eu["2024"]["GDP_Billion_EUR"]) * 100
print(f"Germany share of EU-27 GDP (proxy, 2024): {ger_share:.1f}%")
germany_weighted_drag = (float(get("Germany","2024")["GDP_Growth_Pct"]) - float(eu["2024"]["GDP_Growth_Pct"]))
print(f"Germany growth vs EU total (2024): {get('Germany','2024')['GDP_Growth_Pct']}% vs {eu['2024']['GDP_Growth_Pct']}% ({germany_weighted_drag:+.1f} pts)")
avg_growth_6 = sum(float(get(c, "2024")["GDP_Growth_Pct"]) for c in countries) / len(countries)
print(f"Simple avg growth of the 6 member states (2024): {avg_growth_6:.1f}% vs EU total {eu['2024']['GDP_Growth_Pct']}%")
avg_growth_23_6 = sum(float(get(c, "2023")["GDP_Growth_Pct"]) for c in countries) / len(countries)
print(f"Simple avg growth of the 6 (2023): {avg_growth_23_6:.1f}% vs EU total {eu['2023']['GDP_Growth_Pct']}%")
